clue.text: Life scientist has come with his bit prepared

indicators.note: the letters of these words are worked up into a new arrangement, as a dish is prepared from raw ingredients

explanation.surface: A laboratory researcher turns up having got his share of the work ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' shuffles COME, HIS and BIT together; 'has' and 'with' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist in the chemistry of living organisms is a scientist of life processes.

clue.text: Cute deer one's lost track of circles in the grass

indicators.note: the deer has mislaid the one, so that letter drops out of the name

parts.note: Bambi is the appealing fawn of the Disney film
one is the Roman numeral I
two rings look like the letters O O

explanation.surface: A sweet fawn wandering in the long grass has lost sight of some rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost track of' removes I from BAMBI, leaving BAMB.
explanation.definitionFit: Bamboo is botanically a giant woody member of the grass family.

clue.text: Unfashionable group making a start

parts.note: something out is no longer in fashion
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: A clique of people no longer in vogue is just beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: The outset is the beginning of an undertaking, its very start.

clue.text: Old coins showing William and Mary?

definitions.meaning: gold pieces worth ten shillings, once part of British currency
the joint monarchs each held half of the shared rule over England

explanation.walkthrough: William III and Mary II reigned jointly from 1689, so each was half of a pair of rulers.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold coin worth half a pound, ten shillings, was minted in Britain for centuries.

clue.text: Spoil view outside poor French city

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage

indicators.note: the view wraps around the poor, so one word sits on either side of the other

parts.note: to see is to view
ill means poor, as in poor health

explanation.surface: An ugly outlook ruins the setting of a run-down French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' looks like it describes the city, but it supplies a word of its own; the city is Marseille, spelt here without the English final S.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Mediterranean port is France's second-largest city.

clue.text: Houses responsible for some noxious emissions

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Suburban homes are blamed for part of the polluting fumes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Houses' alone: 'responsible for' only links it to the hidden-word wordplay, and 'Houses responsible' could not stand for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Semis is the British shorthand for semi-detached houses, pairs sharing one wall.

clue.text: Fellow's skin problem

definitions.meaning: to become cracked and sore through cold or wind

explanation.surface: A man's complaint about his dermatitis.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap means a man informally, and also roughened, cracked skin from cold weather.

clue.text: Sidekick of tennis player outside church

indicators.note: the player's name stands around the church abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: Tim Henman, the British player of the 1990s and 2000s

explanation.surface: A tennis star's assistant waits outside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Tim Henman was Britain's leading men's tennis player around 2000, a Wimbledon favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A henchman is a loyal follower or right-hand helper, often to a villain.

clue.text: Describes harbour with fish

parts.note: a port is a harbour
rays are flat cartilaginous fish

explanation.surface: Someone writes about a quayside teeming with fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray someone is to depict or describe them in words or pictures.

clue.text: In need of being buoyed up, unable to cope

definitions.text: In need of being buoyed up
definitions.meaning: in water too deep to stand in, so needing to float
faced with something beyond one's competence

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means literally in water too deep to touch bottom and figuratively overwhelmed.

clue.text: Male, deceased, recalled as good conductor

indicators.note: called back, so the word for deceased is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the late person is one who has died

explanation.surface: A dead man is remembered as a fine orchestra leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns LATE into ETAL; 'good conductor' means of electricity and heat, not music.
explanation.definitionFit: Metals are typically excellent conductors of electricity and heat.

clue.text: Smuggler could be odd fish

parts.note: rum is a British informal word for odd or strange
a runner is a fast-swimming marine fish of the jack family

explanation.surface: A contraband dealer might be a strange sort of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum meaning odd is old-fashioned British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum-runner smuggled alcohol, especially during US Prohibition.

clue.text: Manage to show love with poetry and love's ending

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
verse is poetry

indicators.note: the final letter of the word love is the one taken

explanation.surface: Someone tries to declare their affection in rhymes ending with love.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise or be in charge of, much as a manager does.

clue.text: Conceal son alongside mum

parts.note: mum is a familiar British word for mother

explanation.surface: A boy is hidden away next to his mother.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother something such as a yawn or feeling is to suppress or hide it.

clue.text: Rebel, no leader concerned with gradual change

indicators.note: the rebel's word loses its opening letter, its head

parts.note: a revolutionary is a rebel against the established order

explanation.surface: An insurgent without a commander favours slow reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no leader' takes the R from REVOLUTIONARY; the irony is that a revolutionary wants sudden change.
explanation.definitionFit: Evolution is slow development over time, so the adjective describes incremental progress.

clue.text: Historical practice makes silly idiot rant

indicators.note: the letters are set out in a foolish, disordered fashion

explanation.surface: An old custom provokes a ridiculous fool's tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' scrambles IDIOT and RANT together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradition is a custom handed down from the past through generations.

clue.text: Arrangement that could make loss paid off

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A settlement that might pay off a debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' shuffles LOSS and PAID; 'paid off' looks like a single phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Disposal can mean the arrangement or placing of things, as at one's disposal.

clue.text: Got free, almost looking embarrassed

indicators.note: the word for free falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to acquit someone in court is to set them free
red, as a blushing face is

explanation.surface: Someone gained something for nothing and is now blushing about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ACQUIT to ACQUI.
explanation.definitionFit: To have acquired something is to have obtained or come by it.

clue.text: Imprisoned in vehicle long time, unruly adolescent catches cold

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the run of vehicle, time and youth seizes the cold letter inside it

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
an era is a long period of time
a Teddy boy, a 1950s British youth tearaway
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A delinquent teenager traps someone in a car for ages while sneezing.
explanation.walkthrough: A Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth known for rowdiness; 'catches' places C inside CARERATED, after CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To be incarcerated is to be locked up in prison or confined.

clue.text: Firm includes a wicked thing, opportunity for gambling

indicators.note: the firm's abbreviation contains the other pieces within it

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a sin is a wicked act

explanation.surface: A company embraces vice as a business opening for betting.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a casino is the place that offers the chance to gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a venue offering chances to play games of chance for money.

clue.text: One insect or another is sat upon by maiden

indicators.note: in a down answer the maiden letter sits on top of the other pieces

parts.note: M is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a maiden over
an ant is a further insect

explanation.surface: Two bugs, one of which a young woman has squashed by sitting on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sat upon by' puts M above ANT and IS in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The praying mantis is a predatory insect with folded forelegs.

clue.text: Epistle-writer's superior communication seen by the old man

indicators.note: the superior and communication pieces come beside the father, after him

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, one's old man
U stands for upper class, socially superior
a line is a short message, as in drop me a line

explanation.surface: A letter writer's grand message is read by Dad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Epistle-writer' is St Paul, author of many New Testament letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to St Paul, whose letters fill the New Testament.

clue.text: Choose to miss bits at either end of the lecture

indicators.text: miss bits at either end of
indicators.note: letters are dropped from both ends of the phrase, leaving a central run

explanation.surface: Someone opts to skip the beginning and end of a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss bits at either end of' removes TH and URE from THELECTURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To elect is to choose, especially by voting.

clue.text: The state of Jones at home with woman

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in
Diana is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A man called Jones's condition when at home with a female companion.
explanation.walkthrough: Indiana Jones is the film archaeologist; 'state' looks like a condition but is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is a Midwestern US state, also the first name of the film hero Jones.

clue.text: Plain green site being redeveloped

indicators.note: the letters are rebuilt into a new layout, as a site is when redeveloped

explanation.surface: A flat open stretch of grassland is being turned into a building site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being redeveloped' rearranges GREEN and SITE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is the vast grassland plain of Tanzania and Kenya.

clue.text: Use a brush, article dipped into an amount of liquid

indicators.note: the article goes inside the measure, as a brush goes into a tin

parts.note: a pint is a measure of liquid
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A decorator dips a brush into a pot of liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dipped into' puts A inside PINT.
explanation.definitionFit: To paint is to apply colour, typically with a brush.

clue.text: Woman in station hugging daughter

indicators.note: the station word wraps around the daughter letter, embracing it

parts.note: lay can mean position or situation, as in the lay of the land

explanation.surface: A mother at a railway station embraces her daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'station' here means position, not a railway stop; 'hugging' puts D inside LAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady is a polite word for any woman.

clue.text: Supporters chant and son is going wild

indicators.note: the letters run riot into a new order, as a crowd goes wild

explanation.surface: Football fans sing while someone's boy gets carried away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going wild' rearranges CHANT, SON and IS; 'Supporters' suggests fans but means posts.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanchions are upright posts or bars that hold up a structure.
